clue.text: Bird man different from others?

parts.note: a diver is a water bird, such as the loon
a gent is a man, short for gentleman

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher is described as an oddball who stands apart from everyone else.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that departs from the usual path or opinion is unlike the rest.

clue.text: Car manufacturer overseen by department somewhere in south London

indicators.note: in a down entry the piece that oversees sits above, so the department abbreviation comes first

parts.note: Ford is the American car maker

explanation.surface: A carmaker is said to be supervised by a government department based in a London district.
explanation.walkthrough: Deptford is a district of south-east London on the Thames, once home to a royal dockyard.
explanation.definitionFit: Deptford is a riverside district in the south-east of the capital, so it is one place there.

clue.text: Planet seen in Vienna, oddly, and the States

indicators.note: oddly means take the odd-numbered letters of the city name, first, third and fifth

parts.note: US is short for the United States

explanation.surface: A planet is spotted in the skies over Vienna and America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes the first, third and fifth letters of Vienna, V, E and N.
explanation.definitionFit: The second planet from the Sun is a celestial body named for the Roman goddess of love.

clue.text: Scouting study in a period of history

indicators.note: in tells us the word for study is placed inside the historical period

parts.note: the Renaissance was the period of European cultural revival from the 14th to 17th centuries
to con is an old word meaning to study or learn by heart

explanation.surface: A piece of research on a historical era is presented as a study of the Scout movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scouting' suggests the youth movement, but here it means military scouting. 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Military reconnaissance is exploring ahead to gather information, the job of a scout.

clue.text: Time up: boy is thrown out

indicators.note: in a down entry up means the word for time is written from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Ted is a boy's name, short for Edward

explanation.surface: Time is called and a lad is ejected, like the end of a match or the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit is to send out or discharge, so what was emitted was expelled.

clue.text: Boozer left in truck

indicators.note: in says the abbreviation for left goes inside the vehicle

parts.note: a tipper is a lorry whose load tips out at the back

explanation.surface: A drunk has been abandoned in the back of a lorry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts L inside TIPPER, between the two P's and the E.
explanation.definitionFit: A tippler is a habitual drinker, and a boozer is one too.

clue.text: In retrospect, part of Lombardy is monotonous

indicators.note: retrospect means looking back, so the letters are read from right to left
part of says the letters lie inside the Italian region's name

explanation.surface: Looking back, some of northern Italy was dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of' finds BARD inside LomBARDy and 'In retrospect' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Drab means dull and colourless, lacking any variety.

clue.text: Worked too hard in fund-raising broadcast

indicators.note: worked means the letters have been shaped or kneaded into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone overdid things during a charity appeal on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worked' rearranges the letters of TOO HARD IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A radiothon is a long radio programme run to collect money for charity, like a telethon on radio.

clue.text: Threatening noise in marsh

indicators.note: in places the word for noise inside the word for marsh

parts.note: a bog is wet marshy ground
a din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: A sinister sound is heard out on the marshes.
explanation.definitionFit: Boding is an adjective for something that foretells evil, ominous or menacing.

clue.text: Suggesting a spot of golf's rather presumptuous

parts.note: putting is a bit of golf, the short strokes on the green
forward means bold or presumptuous in manner

explanation.surface: Someone proposing a round of mini-golf is thought a bit cheeky.
explanation.definitionFit: To put forward an idea is to propose it for consideration.

clue.text: Alarm clock initially set by father before turning in

indicators.note: before puts the father's word ahead of the next piece
set by places the remaining letter alongside the rest, at the end

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: turning means the little word is spun round
initially takes just the first letter of the word clock

explanation.surface: An alarm clock is set by Dad before he turns in for the night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' makes NI from IN, and 'initially' gives C from clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Panic is sudden fear, the same as alarm in its sense of fright.

clue.text: 1'I'm beaten and kept in confinement

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
pounded means beaten repeatedly

explanation.surface: Someone complains of being beaten up and locked away.
explanation.definitionFit: Impounded goods or animals are seized and held in an enclosure, shut away.

clue.text: Husband involved in developing finest type of fabric

indicators.note: involved in places the letter for husband inside the other letters
developing means the letters are changing into a new shape

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for husband in genealogy

explanation.surface: A husband takes part in creating the best kind of cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of the clue's 'finest' is FISNET; 'involved in' then works the husband's letter into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Fishnet is an open mesh material, often used for stockings.

clue.text: The French town centre is deserted: that's a disappointment

annotationWithheld.why: The French town centre is deserted: that's a disappointment (3-4). LE + T, D, OWN needs D (deserted) put in TOWN after the T, which is not its centre; no parse or reprint found that accounts for 'centre' and 'deserted'
annotationWithheld.clue: The French town centre is deserted: that's a disappointment

clue.text: Entirely basic requirements for plane, perhaps?

explanation.surface: Something is declared total, then a tree is described by what it needs.
explanation.walkthrough: The plane here is the plane tree, not an aircraft or a tool; a tree's basic parts are its roots and branches.
explanation.definitionFit: Root and branch means completely or thoroughly, as in reform; and roots and branches are what any tree such as a plane must have.

clue.text: Part that's essential in repair of mostly old, big boat

indicators.note: repair means the pieces are refitted in a new order
mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An essential part is needed to fix an old, large vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts OLD to OL; 'repair of' rearranges OL, BIG and BOAT. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In music an obbligato is an accompanying part that must not be left out.

clue.text: Endless loud bangs heard in US stronghold

indicators.note: endless removes the final letter of the musical term

parts.note: forte is the musical direction for loud

indicators.note: heard says the word for bangs is spoken, giving a different spelling

parts.note: knocks are bangs or raps

explanation.surface: Loud explosions ring out at a heavily guarded American base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' trims FORTE to FORT; 'heard' gives KNOCKS, which sounds like KNOX. Fort Knox in Kentucky holds the US gold reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Fort Knox is a US Army post famous for the heavily guarded gold vault there.

clue.text: Out of bounds for soap opera star?

indicators.note: out of means the letters are taken from these words and remade

explanation.surface: A forbidden zone is announced for a soap-opera celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of bounds' looks like a single phrase, but 'Out of' is the anagram signal and BOUNDS FOR SOAP is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A basso profundo is a singer with a very deep bass voice, a possible star of opera.

clue.text: GP, one darting about in the beginning?

indicators.note: darting about means the letters move around into a new order

explanation.surface: A family doctor is spotted rushing around at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'darting about' rearranges GP, ONE and IN.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening is a start, the first stage of something.

clue.text: Four from Germany entering valley in Mediterranean region

indicators.note: entering means the German word goes inside the word for valley

parts.note: a ria is a long narrow inlet formed by a drowned river valley
vier is German for four

explanation.surface: Four German visitors walk into a valley on the Mediterranean coast.
explanation.walkthrough: A ria is an inlet found on drowned coasts, such as in Galicia or Cornwall. 'entering' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Riviera is the coastal strip of south-east France and north-west Italy.

clue.text: Mocks items for consumption

explanation.definitionFit: To scoff is to jeer at; scoff is also slang for food, so plural scoffs are things to eat.

clue.text: Business in time makes money

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A firm that lasts for years makes plenty of cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Coinage is the coins in circulation, a form of currency.

clue.text: Queen today is in very tense state

indicators.note: is in places the queen and the day inside the two abbreviations

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, a queen
today is taken as Monday, abbreviated MON

explanation.surface: The queen is now in a very nervous condition.
explanation.walkthrough: MON is Monday, presumably the day this puzzle ran.
explanation.definitionFit: Vermont is one of the fifty United States, in New England.

clue.text: System of command?

explanation.definitionFit: An order is an arrangement or system, and an order is also an instruction to be obeyed.

clue.text: European country protecting man's right to vote

indicators.note: protecting means the country's name surrounds the possessive

parts.note: France is a country in Europe
his means belonging to a man

explanation.surface: France guards the vote belonging to its menfolk.
explanation.definitionFit: The franchise is suffrage, the entitlement to take part in elections.

clue.text: A degree given by member of university staff is peripheral

parts.note: a don is a university teacher, especially at Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: An academic awards a qualification that turns out to be of marginal value.
explanation.definitionFit: An add-on is an extra, supplementary rather than central.

clue.text: Guess marksman's exhausted

explanation.definitionFit: A shot is an attempt or guess; a good shot is a skilled marksman; shot also means worn out.

clue.text: Very good pair to lead team back in competition

parts.note: grand means excellent or very good

indicators.note: back means the team's Roman numeral is turned round

parts.note: XI, eleven, is a cricket or football team

explanation.surface: A fine couple are put in charge of a side returning to the contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand prix is a major motor race, or a top prize event in other sports.
